## My request for Codex:
Why 4 buffers?
prev_agent:
Added a persistent RX bounce pool so the RTL8139 interrupt path no longer spills packet data onto whatever kernel stack happens to be active. `src/drivers/rtl8139.c:118-157` now pre-allocates four DMA-safe buffers with simple atomic acquire/release helpers, and `rtl8139_handle_receive` copies every frame into one of those buffers before parsing it. That let me delete the stack-based header scratch space; VLAN stripping, tracing, and dispatch now work directly on the bounce buffer. Each loop iteration releases the buffer before advancing the hardware ring so ownership is always clear.

Testing:
- `make -j8` (existing warnings about unused helper functions in `rtl8139.c` remain unchanged).
